issue_context.title: systemd merges deps of mount unit files and /proc/self/mountinfo, leading to surprising results: systemd automatically unmounts manually mounted filesystems [Take #2]
issue_context.body:
PR https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/19322 is supposed to fix issue https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/9869 but AFAICS it's not the case.

IIUC StopPropagatedFrom= is supposed to address the aforementioned issue but I fail to see how exactly: as long as the dependency on the wrong device is still included in the mount dependencies, the problem isn't solved.

The fact that the dependency on the device is now edge-triggered doesn't help, it just moves the problem when the wrong device (the one PID1 initially tracked when the generated mount unit was loaded) is being stopped now.
comments: Since issue https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/9869 had label `v249`, I also put the same label on this issue since both issue are identical.
I can't parse this. Please describe remaining problem precisely and provide a reproducer.

Let's say that fstab has an entry for device `dev-A` which should be mounted on path  /my/mount/unit.

The user unmounts `dev-A` and manually mounts device `dev-B` on /my/mount/unit.

At that point `my-mount-unit.mount` has dependencies on 2 different devices: `dev-A` and `dev-B`.

If for any reason `dev-A` is unplugged,  `my-mount-unit.mount` will be stopped and thus `dev-B` will be incorrectly unmounted.

So as long as `my-mount-unit.mount` will keep a dependency on `dev-A`, the problem remains, no ?

Here's a test case:

```
# systemctl --version
systemd 248 (248-1661-ge4948b0)

# tail -n1 /etc/fstab
/dev/mapper/vdb /mnt  ext4 defaults 1 2

# cat /etc/crypttab
vdb  UUID=289d7e97-deac-4769-bb7f-991e4c66814a none discard
vdc  UUID=ffda7bac-7437-46d6-a01a-512930f64041 none discard

# systemctl status mnt.mount 
● mnt.mount - /mnt
     Loaded: loaded (/etc/fstab; generated)
     Active: active (mounted) since Mon 2021-06-21 14:47:48 CEST; 3min 10s ago
      Where: /mnt
       What: /dev/mapper/vdb
      [...]

# umount /mnt 
# mount /dev/mapper/vdc /mnt/
# systemctl status mnt.mount 
● mnt.mount - /mnt
     Loaded: loaded (/etc/fstab; generated)
     Active: active (mounted) since Mon 2021-06-21 14:51:40 CEST; 4s ago
      Where: /mnt
       What: /dev/mapper/vdc
      [...]

# systemctl stop systemd-cryptsetup@vdb.service 
# systemctl status mnt.mount 
○ mnt.mount - /mnt
     Loaded: loaded (/etc/fstab; generated)
     Active: inactive (dead) since Mon 2021-06-21 14:53:02 CEST; 2s ago
      Where: /mnt
       What: /dev/mapper/vdb
       Docs: man:fstab(5)
             man:systemd-fstab-generator(8)
        CPU: 3ms

Jun 21 14:53:02 vm-tumbleweed systemd[1]: Unmounting /mnt...
Jun 21 14:53:02 vm-tumbleweed systemd[1]: mnt.mount: Deactivated successfully.
Jun 21 14:53:02 vm-tumbleweed systemd[1]: Unmounted /mnt.

```

I believe this issue here goes back to the issue https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/1741 (and fixing it would likely close this old and heatedly discussed bug :see_no_evil: ).

See my post to the ML about it: https://lists.freedesktop.org/archives/systemd-devel/2021-July/046671.html

review_comments: Can you explain the need for this new flag please, I'm not following. What problem is this commit supposed to solve exactly ?

Yeah, this seems strange. This flag seems to be essentially saying "we don't know where this dependency came from exactly". It breaks the orthogonality of the different flags. After reading the commit message, I'd expect that we simply propagate the information about the appropriate mask from the caller down into the functions adding the dependencies. If they are added based on the unit file, use one mask; if they are added based on mountinfo, use the other mask.

Strictly speaking, the dependencies tagged with this new label _always_ depend on /proc/self/mountinfo in some sense. Of course, if there exists a relevant entry in /proc/self/mountinfo, then the dependencies depend on it. Even if there is _no_ corresponding entry in /proc/self/mountinfo, the dependencies _are_ based on the fact that there is no entry in /proc/self/mountinfo. Hence, when /proc/self/mountinfo is updated, we need to regenerate the dependencies, and they must not be labeled with `UNIT_DEPENDENCY_FILE`.

Though, the name `UNIT_DEPENDENCY_MOUNTINFO_OR_FILE` may be misleading. But I have no idea about better name. Do you have any suggestions?
